pages.text: Some tobacco styles build on an existing cure and then receive a longer finishing treatment. The finished tobacco reports the traditional name directly in its $(thing)Cure$() field rather than adding another technical tooltip.

pages.title: Latakia
pages.text: Start with $(item)Sun-Cured Oriental$() leaf. Return it to a Drying Rack or hanging bunch and expose it to $(item)ordinary Campfire smoke$() for an extended finishing cycle. The result becomes $(thing)Latakia$(). With Create, smoking airflow from an Encased Fan can perform the same finish.

pages.title: Dark Fired Kentucky
pages.text: Start with $(item)Fire-Cured Burley$(). Give it a second, extended ordinary-smoke finish on a rack or hanging bunch to produce $(thing)Dark Fired Kentucky$(). Create smoking airflow is also valid.

pages.title: Why Named Cures?
pages.text: These results are more specific than simply calling tobacco Sun-Cured or Fire-Cured. Variety and processing both matter, so the final Cure field changes to the traditional style name when the complete process succeeds.
